title: Nature of Light

description.main: Nature of Light is the catalogue of the exhibition that opened Izu Photo Museum in October 2009, a building whose interior and courtyard Hiroshi Sugimoto designed himself, and it presents two new series made in homage to William Henry Fox Talbot. Texts by Sugimoto, Larry J. Schaaf and Minoru Shimizu, in Japanese and English.
description.extended:
Nature of Light is the catalogue of the exhibition that opened Izu Photo Museum in October 2009, a building whose interior and courtyard Hiroshi Sugimoto designed himself, and it presents two new series made in homage to William Henry Fox Talbot.

The Lightning Fields are made without a camera by discharging static electricity onto film, and the book follows them from early tests to the fifteen-metre work shown at the opening. The Photogenic Drawings print fifteen of Talbot's paper negatives from the 1830s and 1840s, unprinted in his lifetime, as enlarged positives. Larry J. Schaaf writes the plate commentary, the critic Minoru Shimizu an essay on the artist, and Sugimoto's own text accompanies the first publication of his work from the 1970s. Photographs of the museum interior and garden record his work as its designer. Japanese and English throughout. Hardcover in a dust jacket, 151 pages, distributed by Nohara.

Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) built his reputation on the Theaters, Seascapes and Dioramas, each a sustained inquiry into what the camera records of time. The Izu exhibition marked his turn toward photography's chemical origins and toward architecture, which later produced the Enoura Observatory in Odawara. The library also holds the Hatje Cantz retrospective catalogue of 2005.
description.artist_bio: Hiroshi Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) has lived and worked in New York since 1974. His series Dioramas, Theaters, Seascapes and Portraits are held by MoMA, the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Guggenheim. Since the mid-2000s he has worked increasingly in architecture and installation, designing the interior of Izu Photo Museum (2009) and the Enoura Observatory in Odawara (2017).
description.exhibition_context: Nature of Light was the inaugural exhibition of Izu Photo Museum at Clematis no Oka, Nagaizumi, Shizuoka, 26 October 2009 to 16 March 2010. It showed the Lightning Fields at their largest scale to date, including a fifteen-metre photogram, with the Photogenic Drawing series after Talbot and a thirteenth-century Raijin sculpture.
